goal: Measure whether two distinct AI model families can choose numerical model parameters that generalize across molecular-solubility regression and public cell-morphology classification.

chemistry.target: measured log solubility in mols per litre
chemistry.excluded_leakage_column: ESOL predicted log solubility in mols per litre
chemistry.split: deterministic Bemis-Murcko scaffold groups (acyclic molecules grouped by exact canonical SMILES)

biology.source: scikit-learn load_breast_cancer (public UCI Wisconsin Diagnostic data)
biology.split: stratified seeded train/development/test, target only used for training/evaluation
biology.task: historical biomedical morphology classification, NOT clinical diagnosis

baselines: scaled linear estimator (ridge for chemistry, logistic regression for biology)
selection: compare both candidate and baseline developmental metric on predefined splits; candidate must reduce validation error by >=2 percent relative to strongest baseline; otherwise retain baseline; preserve rejected proposals
execution: CPU GitHub Actions with separate candidate jobs, independent development verification and held-out audit; archive successes and failures to research-memory
limitations: historical public data can have appeared in model pretraining
bio data are research only, not clinically validated
ESOL scaffold split mitigates but does not eliminate analogue leakage
a better benchmark score is not scientific invention, autonomous general intelligence, or recursive self-improvement
no arbitrary generated code, no paid services, no model promotions
proposals are bounded hyperparameter choices in prewritten model classes
